facts.text: On this date in 1066, William the Conqueror landed in England — permanently shifting the English language. About 30% of modern English words trace directly to the Norman French his invasion introduced.

On this date in 1994, the ferry Estonia sank in the Baltic Sea, killing 852 people. It remains Europe's deadliest peacetime maritime disaster since WWII, yet it happened just 22 miles from Swedish waters.
Monaco is so densely packed — 26,000 people per square kilometer — that if the entire world lived at that density, every human on Earth would fit inside the state of Rhode Island.
More people live in Tokyo's greater metropolitan area than in all of Canada. At 37 million residents, it is the largest urban agglomeration in recorded human history.
The Maldives has the lowest average elevation of any country on Earth — just 1.8 meters above sea level. Its entire national territory could be rendered uninhabitable within a single human lifetime.
On this date in 1929, the London Stock Exchange suspended trading after panic selling spread from New York — a week before Black Tuesday made the crash official history.
On this date in 2008, the U.S. House rejected the $700B TARP bailout, triggering the single largest point drop in Dow history at the time: 777 points in one session.
The NYSE's famously chaotic open-outcry trading floor was, until the 1870s, conducted entirely outdoors on the sidewalk of Wall Street.
Saudi Aramco briefly surpassed $2 trillion in market cap on its 2019 IPO day — then spent the next three years below that figure, making the milestone mostly ceremonial.
The term 'bear market' likely traces to 18th-century bearskin traders who sold pelts they didn't yet own, betting prices would fall before delivery — short selling by another name.

On this date in 1889, the international kilogram prototype was officially sanctioned — a cylinder of platinum-iridium that defined mass for 130 years until a 2019 vote replaced it with a fixed mathematical constant.

On this date in 2003, the SMART-1 spacecraft left Earth using an ion thruster, accelerating by firing charged xenon atoms — the same physics that governs a rocket, but so gentle it took 13 months to reach the Moon.
Your skeleton is not static. Osteoclasts dissolve old bone while osteoblasts rebuild it, replacing your entire skeleton roughly every decade.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its matter would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
The mantis shrimp sees with 16 types of color receptors — humans have 3 — yet research shows it processes color worse than we do, suggesting more channels does not mean richer perception.
On this day in 1066, William the Conqueror landed in England. The Norman invasion he launched is closer in time to the fall of Rome than it is to us today.
Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. The pyramid is simply that old.
On this day in 1928, Alexander Fleming noticed mold killing bacteria in a petri dish. He almost discarded the plate.
The fax machine was patented in 1843, before the American Civil War, before the telephone, and a full 26 years before the transcontinental railroad was completed.
On this day in 1542, Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo became the first European to set foot on the California coast. Los Angeles would not be a U.S. city for another 307 years.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in 2012, it spread so fast it feels ancient.
Hiraeth (Welsh): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to — or one that never existed. No single English word comes close.
On this day in 1066, William the Conqueror landed at Pevensey. He brought Norman French with him, and English has never recovered — nearly half its vocabulary still bears the wound.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Another Koenig coinage, yet it names something everyone has felt and no older language bothered to capture.
On September 28, 1928, Alexander Fleming noticed mold killing bacteria in a petri dish. The word 'antibiotic' — from Greek anti + bios, against life — was coined a decade later by Selman Waksman.

On this date in 2022, Ethereum completed its merge from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake, cutting the network's energy consumption by ~99.95% overnight — the largest infrastructure migration in crypto history.
On Sept 28, 2021, the EU Parliament's ECON committee voted down a proposed PoW mining ban that would have effectively outlawed Bitcoin in Europe.

Bitcoin's 21 million supply cap is enforced by integer arithmetic, not policy. Miners receive block subsidies in satoshis; the halving loop simply shifts a bit right until the reward rounds to zero around 2140.

The DAO hack of 2016 drained 3.6 million ETH through a reentrancy bug — the attacker's funds sat locked for weeks because The DAO's own code imposed a 28-day withdrawal delay, giving Ethereum time to fork.

Satoshi's genesis block coinbase contains the text 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — both a timestamp and a statement of intent, embedded permanently in Bitcoin's chain.

On this date in 2015, Google DeepMind's Atari paper appeared in Nature — the first time a single agent matched human performance across 49 games using only raw pixels and reward signals, no hand-crafted features.

On this date in 2022, DeepMind released AlphaTensor, which discovered matrix multiplication algorithms faster than any known to mathematicians — solving a problem open since Strassen's 1969 breakthrough.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US households, for a single model training pass.
The transformer architecture, now underlying most frontier AI systems, was published in 2017 by eight Google researchers. Six of the eight have since left Google, several to found competing AI labs.

RLHF — the technique that made ChatGPT feel cooperative rather than erratic — was first demonstrated not on language models but on simulated robot locomotion tasks, in a 2017 OpenAI and DeepMind paper.
